hook_text: Drop a 2 kg ball and a 5 kg ball off the same roof. They land at EXACTLY the same speed. Here's the accounting trick that proves it.
clip_script: Picture a wallet with exactly two pockets. The first pocket is the height pocket: money goes in whenever the object climbs. The second is the speed pocket: money goes in whenever the object moves faster. Here is the rule the whole lesson stands on: as long as nothing rubs — no friction, no air resistance — the wallet is sealed. Money can move between the two pockets as often as it likes, but not one cent can enter or leave. Drop something, and coins stream from the height pocket into the speed pocket the whole way down. The total never budges.
visual_style: A wallet with two glowing pockets beside a falling ball; coins stream from the height pocket to the speed pocket as the ball drops, with the total counter frozen at 392 J.
pacing: Calm setup of the two pockets, then accelerating coin-flow synced to the fall, freeze on the unchanged total.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and count the ball's wallet from rooftop to ground.
